links.outcome: Hallucination rate with DSM-5 knowledge-graph grounding versus standard prompting
links.effect: The DSM-5-guided structured knowledge graph significantly reduced hallucinations compared to standard prompting. Top-1 diagnostic accuracy was 85.6%, 15-54 percentage points above knowledge-enhanced single-agent baselines.
links.quote: Our framework utilizes a Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5)-guided Structured Knowledge Graph to steer diagnostic inquiries, significantly reducing hallucinations compared to standard prompting methods.

unlisted_practices: Dialectical Behavior Therapy-inspired multi-agent design pairing a reasoning agent with an empathetic communication agent
Knowledge-graph-guided diagnostic questioning for psychiatric assessment

screen.reason: The paper introduces and benchmarks a novel multi-agent system (WiseMind) using structured knowledge graphs and simulated/real user sessions for psychiatric diagnosis, but tests model performance rather than a specific deployment guardrail practice.
